BIOC 202.title: Introductory Medical Biochemistry
BIOC 202.description: Introduction to proteins and enzymes, carbohydrate metabolism, and glucose homeostasis. The course emphasis is on human biochemistry and it is designed for students going into health science fields.

BIOC 203.title: Fundamentals of Biochemistry
BIOC 203.description: Amino acids and proteins. Enzymes and enzymology. Human metabolic pathways. Structure, function and metabolism of carbohydrates including glycogen storage and gluconeogenesis. Restricted to students in Biochemistry specializations.
BIOC 203.prerequisiteText: BIOL 200 and one of CHEM 203, CHEM 223

BIOC 301.title: Biochemistry Laboratory
BIOC 301.description: Techniques by which the chemical and physical properties of fundamental components of the cell are studied.

children.raw: third-year class standing or higher in Biochemistry
third-year class standing or higher in Pharmacology

BIOC 301.prerequisiteText: Either (a) CHEM_V 245 and third-year class standing or higher in Biochemistry or (b) CHEM_V 235 and third-year class standing or higher in Pharmacology

BIOC 302.title: General Biochemistry
BIOC 302.description: Metabolic reactions of lipids, steroids, amino acids and nucleotides; the biochemistry of replication, transcription and translation.
BIOC 302.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203 and one of CHEM 203, CHEM 223, CHEM 233

BIOC 303.title: Molecular Biochemistry
BIOC 303.description: Structure, function and metabolism of lipids, steroids, amino acids and nucleotides; the biochemistry and molecular biology of replication, transcription, translation and gene regulation. For students in Biochemistry and Honours programs in other life sciences.
BIOC 303.prerequisiteText: One of BIOC 203, BIOC 202, BIOL 201 and either (a) CHEM 213 or (b) CHEM 233

BIOC 304.title: Contemporary Biochemical Research
BIOC 304.description: Exploration of the breadth and importance of biochemical research to present day challenges in medicine and biotechnology. Detailed experimental research case studies of novel biochemical methods used to address pressing and ongoing biochemical issues.

BIOC 306.title: Quantitative Methods in Biochemistry
BIOC 306.description: Quantitative and computational methods of biological information transfer. Methods; data analysis approaches and theories involved in bioinformatics; computational biology and high-throughput data.

children.raw: with a grade of 76% or higher and a corequisite of

BIOC 306.prerequisiteText: a) BIOC 203 and a corequisite of BIOC 303 or b) One of BIOC 202 or BIOL 201 with a grade of 76% or higher and a corequisite of BIOC 302

BIOC 398.title: Internship Work Placement I
BIOC 398.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial or academic laboratory for three or four months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Internship Program in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology.

prerequisite.raw: Completion of academic third year in Biochemistry major or honours program is required

BIOC 398.prerequisiteText: Completion of academic third year in Biochemistry major or honours program is required

BIOC 399.title: Internship Work Placement II
BIOC 399.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial or academic research setting for four months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Internship Program in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology.

BIOC 402.title: Proteins: Structure and Function
BIOC 402.description: Structural components of proteins, classification by primary, secondary and tertiary structure, protein chemistry and purification, peptide and protein synthesis by chemical means and three-dimensional structure determination using X-ray diffraction and NMR.
notes: A minimum standing of 65% is recommended in these courses.

BIOC 403.title: Enzymology
BIOC 403.description: Kinetic analysis, catalytic mechanisms, transition state stabilization and regulation of activity, strategies for active site characterization and case studies of well-documented enzyme systems.
notes: BIOC402 A minimum standing of 65% is recommended.

BIOC 404.title: Biochemical Methods
BIOC 404.description: Theory and application of classical and emerging technologies in biochemical research. Emphasis on using primary literature and oral presentation skills. Restricted to Honours students in Biochemistry or others with permission of the instructor.

BIOC 410.title: Nucleic Acids-Structure and Function
BIOC 410.description: Chemical, physical and biological properties of nucleic acids and their role in replication, transcription, translation and regulation of expression of genetic material.
BIOC 410.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of BIOC 303, BIOL 335 or (b) BIOT 380
notes: A minimum standing of 65% is recommended in these courses.

BIOC 420.title: Advanced Biochemical Techniques
BIOC 420.description: Multi-week experiments in areas of contemporary biochemistry research using classical and modern techniques. Emphasis on experimental design, technique, critical analysis of data, and scientific communication skills. Restricted to Honours students in Biochemistry and others with permission of the instructor.

BIOC 421.title: Recombinant DNA Techniques
BIOC 421.description: Multi-week experiments involving contemporary nucleic acid research, cloning and recombinant protein engineering. Emphasis is on experimental design, critical analysis of data and scientific communication skills. Restricted to Major students in Biochemistry.

BIOC 430.title: Advanced Topics in Protein Biochemistry
BIOC 430.description: Advanced topics in protein structure and function.

BIOC 440.title: Concepts in Molecular Biology
BIOC 440.description: Developing areas of molecular biology, focusing on experimental design and data analysis. Signal transduction, the use of model eukaryotes, and the regulation of gene expression.
BIOC 440.prerequisiteText: One of BIOC 303, BIOT 380 and all of BIOC 402, BIOC 410

BIOC 448.title: Directed Studies in Biochemistry
BIOC 448.description: A library (3 credits) or a laboratory project with written report (3 or 6 credits) allowing a student to undertake an investigation on a specific topic as agreed upon by the faculty and student.

prerequisite.raw: Permission of the Department Head is required

BIOC 448.prerequisiteText: Permission of the Department Head is required

BIOC 449.title: Honours Thesis
BIOC 449.description: A research problem under the direction of a faculty member. Restricted to Honours students.

BIOC 450.title: Membrane Biochemistry
BIOC 450.description: Biochemistry of membranes and membrane proteins, membrane fusion, electrical signaling, and the involvement of membrane proteins in disease and drug development.
BIOC 450.prerequisiteText: One of BIOC 303, BIOT 380 and all of BIOC 402, BIOC 410

BIOC 460.title: Advanced Techniques in Biochemistry
BIOC 460.description: Theoretical basis and practical applications of a selection of advanced techniques currently used in biochemical research. Topics will vary.
BIOC 460.prerequisiteText: One of BIOC 303, BIOT 380 and all of BIOC 402, BIOC 410

BIOC 470.title: Biochemistry & Society: Current Issues
BIOC 470.description: Biochemical basis of select global challenges. Critical evaluation of primary literature to form evidence-based opinions and communicating biochemistry as it relates to several controversial societal issues.

BIOC 490.title: Student Directed Seminars
BIOC 490.description: Self-directed, collaborative studies, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment, and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. Not given every year.

BIOC 498.title: Internship Work Placement III
BIOC 498.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial or academic research setting for four months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Internship Program in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology.

BIOC 499.title: Internship Work Placement IV
BIOC 499.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial or academic research setting for four months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Internship Program in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology.

BIOC 501.title: Advanced Biochemistry Laboratory
BIOC 501.description: Practical applications of advanced biochemical techniques. Admission is limited and is by permission of the department head.

BIOC 509.title: Membrane Structure and Function
BIOC 509.description: The physical properties and functional roles of lipids in membranes, liposomes, membrane permiability; membrane function; structure, biosynthesis and cell sorting of membrane proteins; and the structure-function relationships of channels, transporters and receptors. Given in alternate years. .

BIOC 510.title: Nucleic Acids: Structure and Function
BIOC 510.description: Structure and function of nucleic acids and their role in replication, transcription, translation and expression of genetic information. .

BIOC 511.title: Biochemical Aspects of Cellular Regulation
BIOC 511.description: A lecture and discussion course on the molecular basis of cellular regulation with special emphasis on mammalian cells. Mechanisms involved in the responses of cells to adrenergic, steroid and peptide hormones and growth factors. Regulation of the concentration and specific activity of key enzymes, transport systems and structural proteins. Given in alternate years. .

BIOC 514.title: Advanced Topics in Protein Chemistry
BIOC 514.description: Topics will include contemporary theoretical and experimental investigation of protein structure-function relationships. Topics will vary. Given in alternate years. .

BIOC 522.title: Membrane Proteins
BIOC 522.description: Structure, biosynthesis and cell sorting of membrane proteins; and the structure-function relationships of channels, transporters and receptors.

BIOC 530.title: Seminar in Biochemistry
BIOC 530.description: Attendance is required of all graduate students in Biochemistry. Normally students will make a presentation once per year on a topic approved by their research advisor or committee or on the results of their research.

BIOC 548.title: Directed Studies
BIOC 548.description: In special cases, with approval of the department head, advanced courses may be arranged for graduate students in attendance.

BIOC 551.title: Advanced Topics in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
BIOC 551.description: Discussions based on topics in the current literature. .

BIOC 552.title: Membrane Proteins
BIOC 552.description: Structure, biosynthesis and cell sorting of membrane proteins; and the structure-function relationships of channels, transporters and receptors.

BIOC 553.title: Advanced Topics in Lipid Biology
BIOC 553.description: Principles of lipid structure and dynamics; biochemical approaches to study lipids and applications of lipid biology.

BIOC 554.title: Nucleic Acids: DNA/RNA Structure and Function
BIOC 554.description: Mechanisms, regulation and dynamics of DNA and RNA biology. Structure and function of nucleic acids and their role in replication, transcription, translation and expression of genetic information.

BIOC 555.title: Epigenetics
BIOC 555.description: Principles, regulation and dynamics of epigenetics.

BIOC 556.title: Biochemical Aspects of Cellular Regulation
BIOC 556.description: Mechanisms involved in the responses of cells to adrenergic, steroid and peptide hormones and growth factors. Recent advances in approaches and regulation of the concentration and specific activity of key enzymes, transport systems and structural proteins. Given in alternate years. .

BIOC 557.title: Advanced Topics in Biochemistry
BIOC 557.description: Advances in biochemical approaches. Topics vary.

BIOC 558.title: Advanced Topics in Protein Chemistry I
BIOC 558.description: Contemporary theoretical and experimental investigation of protein structure-function relationships. Topics will vary.

BIOC 559.title: Advanced Topics in Protein Chemistry II
BIOC 559.description: Contemporary theoretical and experimental investigation of protein structure-function relationships. Topics will vary.

BIOC 560.title: Computational Approaches in Biochemistry
BIOC 560.description: Computational approaches to study protein and nucleic acids.
